Performers
Marian Anderson (contralto), Kosti Vehanen (piano) Documented

The Discography of American Historical Recordings lists Anderson as vocalist (contralto) and Vehanen as pianist, and describes the matrix as a contralto vocal solo with piano. The Internet Archive creator field lists Price, Anderson and Vehanen.

[3] [1]
Work version
Price’s arrangement for voice and piano, as sung by Marian Anderson on Victor 1799. The disc label gives the title as “My Soul’s Been Anchored in the Lord”. Inferred, not documented

The Discography of American Historical Recordings names Florence Price as arranger, from the disc label, and the Remick edition of 1937 is annotated “As sung by Marian Anderson (Victor Record No. 1799)”. Which printed or manuscript version the singer and pianist used (key, cuts, ending) is not stated, and neither the Remick nor the Gamble edition was seen. The Internet Archive file is titled “My Souls Been Anchored In The Lord”.

[3] [7] [1]
Recorded
1936-02-04 Documented

Matrix BS-99538 was recorded on 4 February 1936; takes 1, 1A, 2 and 2A are listed for that day and take 2 is the master issued on Victor 1799 and Gramophone DA-1560. The Internet Archive date of 1937 is the year of release, not of the session.

[3]
Place
New York, New York, Studio 3 Documented

As given for every take of the matrix in the Discography of American Historical Recordings.

[3]
Label
Victor (Camden, N.J.), 10-inch double-faced Red Seal; the same take was issued as Gramophone DA-1560 Documented

The Discography of American Historical Recordings describes Victor 1799 as a 10-inch double-faced Red Seal and lists the same two matrices under Gramophone DA-1560. The Internet Archive item gives the publisher as Victor.

[4] [5] [1]
Catalogue
Victor 1799, side B (coupled with Burleigh’s “Go Down, Moses”, matrix BS-99537); released February 1937 Documented

Release date 2/1937 is given by the Discography of American Historical Recordings from the Victor catalogue. The American Record Guide reviewed the disc in February 1937 at $1.50. The Internet Archive item records the side as “1799-B”, which is the label side designation; its “Matrix number: 1799B” is not a Victor matrix number.

[4] [6] [1]
Matrix, take, sides
BS-99538, take 2 Documented

Take 2 is the master issued on Victor 1799 and on Gramophone DA-1560. That the Internet Archive transfer is of the Victor 1799 pressing rests on the item’s description (“Victor (1799-B)”).

[3]
Transfer
Digitised by George Blood, L.P. for the Internet Archive’s Great 78 Project Documented

The item metadata gives George Blood, L.P. as the scanning centre and the item belongs to the collections 78rpm, georgeblood, archiveofcontemporarymusic and audio_music.

[2]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

The Internet Archive lists the item as added on 11 February 2017; that is the upload, not the date of the transfer.

[2]
Processing
Four styli (2.0, 2.3, 2.8 and 3.3 mil truncated conical) were used; the transfers were made flat and also equalised with a turnover of 500. The preferred version is the equalised transfer with the 2.3 mil stylus, copied as the file used here (named “restored”). Documented

From the item description. Noise reduction and any speed correction are not described.

[2]
Composition rights
Price died on 3 June 1953, so her arrangement has been out of copyright in the EU and the United Kingdom (life plus 70 years) since 1 January 2024. In the United States it was registered for copyright on 12 August 1937 by Gamble Hinged Music Co.; whether that copyright was renewed was not checked. The underlying spiritual is traditional. Inferred, not documented

The registration is documented by the Price Works Catalog. The EU term is a calculation from her death date, which the composer chapter on this site gives. Rights in the composition are separate from rights in the recording and do not block publication.

[7]
Recording rights
Territorial EU public domain: first published before 1963 (Victor 1799, released February 1937). United States status not established: a recording first published in 1937 is still within the term of federal protection for pre-1972 recordings, and the Internet Archive item sits in the collection that was the subject of UMG Recordings, Inc. v. Internet Archive. Documented

The release date comes from the Victor catalogue as given by the Discography of American Historical Recordings, and a review of the disc appeared in February 1937. For recordings first published between 1923 and 1946 the Copyright Office describes a term of 95 years plus 5 years after first publication, which for 1937 runs to the end of 2037. The Great 78 Project was the subject of a lawsuit by record companies, settled confidentially in September 2025 (reported by Music Business Worldwide, and acknowledged by the Internet Archive on 15 September 2025); its terms were not published. The item’s curation note of 22 August 2025 reads “lawsuit temporary undark and noindex”: the item was restored to view but is withheld from search indexing. On 19 October 2026 the Internet Archive record of the British pressing of the same take (HMV DA 1560, item 78_my-souls-been-anchored-in-the-lord_marian-anderson-kosti-vehanen-price_gbia0125732b) was marked dark. If the Internet Archive withdraws this item, the stream will fail.

[4] [6] [10] [11] [12] [2]

Florence Price, My Soul’s Been Anchored in de Lord (arrangement for voice and piano). Marian Anderson, contralto; Kosti Vehanen, piano. Recorded 4 February 1936, New York (Victor matrix BS-99538, take 2); issued on Victor 1799 in February 1937. Transfer by George Blood, L.P. for the Internet Archive’s Great 78 Project, item 78_my-souls-been-anchored-in-the-lord_florence-b.-price-marian-anderson-kosti-vehanen_gbia0000781b. Territorial EU basis (first published before 1963); US status not established. Rights statement
